---
title: "Trade policy Trump 2.0 and US trade"
description: "Tariff uncertainty widened, rather than narrowed, the US trade deficit in early 2025, as stockpiling of gold, semiconductors, and pharmaceutical inputs inflated imports."
date: "2025-08-08"
categories: [trade-wars]
---

Rather than shrinking the deficit as intended, Trump's protectionist agenda coincided with a stockpiling boom — a $71 billion surge in gold imports plus heavy buying of semiconductors and pharmaceutical hormones from Ireland — that pushed the average monthly US trade deficit to around $115 billion. The piece frames this as part of a broader shift away from the rules-based multilateral trading system toward bilateral deals and fragmentation, with the fuller costs still to land as more tariffs take effect from August 2025 onward.

**Originally published on Substack**, August 8, 2025.
